subject: URGENT: SageWell production slowdown after v5.2 quant flip
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sagewell.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@sagewell.com
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: sudden latency & 5xx spike after v5.2 quant change

Sergio / Marissa —

We just flipped SageWell production to Redwood model v5.2 with the new qint8-fast quant profile at 07:50 PT and immediately started seeing p95 latency double and a surge in 500s. Throughput dropped ~40% and our front-end queue is backing up. Attachments: sagewell_logs_0904.zip (stack traces + sample requests).

Key metrics since the flip (last 15m):
- p50: ~120ms -> 150ms (+25%)
- p95: 420ms -> 1.1s (+160%)
- error rate (5xx): 0.3% -> 8.7%
- RPS: 1,200 -> 720

This is customer-critical as multiple checkout flows are timing out. We need a rollback if you can support that immediately, or a safe fallback to a pre-flip variant. Please advise ETA — we will open an incident on our side as well.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
VP Product Ops, SageWell
alex.turner@sagewell.com

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sagewell.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@sagewell.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 09:05:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency & 5xx spike after v5.2 quant change

Alex — thanks for the heads-up and for the logs. We're treating this as Sev1.

Immediate actions we are initiating now:
1) Rollback path: scheduling a rollback to v5.1 (previously stable) — targeting 09:25 PT.
2) Routing fallback: enabling model-variant fallback (v5.1) at the load balancer to drain hotpath traffic while rollback proceeds.
3) Ops runbook: I've attached the incident runbook we will follow (incident_runbook_v2.pdf).
4) Exec loop: looping in Platform and Engineering leads (Irene + Aditya) for RCA and mitigation plan; we will brief your CTO after stabilization.

Can you confirm: is there a specific traffic slice we should avoid flipping (e.g., premium customers / payments)? Also, please share whether you have any pinned model variants or traffic-splitting rules on your side.

Irene / Aditya — please triage kernel/quantization signals (decode stalls, kernel fallbacks) and confirm whether this looks like increased compute per-token (leading to queueing) or a correctness-related retry pattern.

I will update every 15 minutes until we either rollback or stabilize.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 13:20:37 -0700
Subject: RE: Production: sudden latency & 5xx spike after v5.2 quant change

Quick technical summary from infra / runtime triage (observed 10:00–12:45 PT):

Observations: 
- The qint8-fast profile we shipped with v5.2 triggers an alternate kernel path for attention decoding that is faster on long sequences but relies on a narrower KV cache alignment. On SageWell's workload (many short messages, high concurrency) we see excessive kernel context switches and repeated small-copy ops.
- Concurrency pattern: token-level CPU/GPU context-switch overhead increased ~2.3x for hotpath requests, small steady-state batches. This produced head-of-line blocking and queueing at the runtime scheduler.
- Error pattern: 500s correlate with timeout/retry on the application layer after backend decode latencies exceeded the request timeout threshold; not a model output correctness failure.

Proposed immediate mitigations (short-term):
A) Roll back to v5.1 (already in progress) — should restore prior kernel path and drop p95 back near baseline.
B) If rollback takes longer: throttle concurrency to reduce small-batch kernel switching, add a per-request decode timeout guard, and divert heavy checkout flows to warm v5.1 pool.
C) Post-mortem actions: refine quant profile heuristics in our build pipeline so qint8-fast is only enabled for workloads with median sequence lengths > 128 and provide an auto-safeguard based on observed kernel switch rates.

I'll push a one-line patch to the quant config to disable the fast path for SageWell's org id and runbench a canary. If rollback completes cleanly we still should plan a warm-replay session with SageWell to validate per-token latencies for candidate quant profiles.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao
Principal Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sagewell.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@sagewell.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Sep 2028 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production: sudden latency & 5xx spike after v5.2 quant change — stabilization update and next steps

Alex / Priya —

Status update and summary for execs: rollback to v5.1 completed at 15:40 PT and SageWell metrics recovered within ~12 minutes. Final observed numbers post-rollback (15:55 PT):
- p95: ~430ms
- error rate (5xx): 0.4%
- RPS: 1,160

What happened: the v5.2 qint8-fast profile introduced a kernel execution path that is beneficial for long-context batches but regresses small-batch, high-concurrency workloads (head-of-line blocking + kernel switch overhead). This resulted in increased per-token latency and application-level timeouts.

Actions taken:
- Immediate: rollback to v5.1; enabled tenant-scoped safeguards to prevent qint8-fast from auto-applying to SageWell until we complete validation.
- Short-term: Aditya pushed a config flag to disable the fast kernel for org id; we will run a controlled canary next week during a low-traffic window (TBD).
- Post-mortem: we will run a joint replay and produce a root-cause doc + action items by EOD Wed 2028-09-07. Executive summary will be shared with your CTO and our CTO.

Compensation / credits: I understand the impact to your users. Sergio and I will follow up with our Finance & Sales Ops teams to propose a service credit for the incident window; we'll route that through your commercial contact (DEAL-8472).

We're scheduling a 30-min technical walk-through tomorrow 10:00 PT to review the telemetries and proposed fixes. Please reply if that time works or propose an alternative.

Apologies again for the disruption — we take this seriously and will be transparent in the post-mortem.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
